summary: Native admission protects configured cgroups from pressure without treating admitted jobs' self-throttling as host distress.

schema.detail: Optional protected, job-parent, and excluded cgroup policy paths and source-path details are added to local pressure evidence. No SQL migration or client-v0 schema change.

rules.detail: Memory and I/O PSI use the maximum over protected cgroups. Defaults protect the daemon service, system.slice, app.slice, and any discovered interactive.slice. Configured job parents cover gate, native lanes, capped, and batch launchers. Protected ancestors are split only along configured job paths, even after job removal, avoiding lingering ancestor PSI. Each sample refreshes that frontier, bounded to 256 cgroup directories and 4096 raw entries with distinct named failures. Vanished children and absent optional discovered roots are skipped; unreadable existing protected files and exceeded bounds fail closed with path-specific evidence. Invalid policy paths are rejected at load. The independent MemAvailable floor, thresholds, sampler cadence, freshness, and recovery hysteresis remain unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Existing policy documents use automatic protected-cgroup defaults. Deploy this version before configuring protectedCgroups, jobParentCgroups, or excludedCgroups, which older daemons do not understand. Existing membership reason records remain readable.

manual.detail: For nonstandard layouts, configure psiBrake.protectedCgroups, jobParentCgroups, and excludedCgroups. Job-parent and exclusion slice unit names resolve to canonical user-manager hierarchies; absolute paths are relative to the cgroup v2 mount. Inspect retained path-specific reasons if discovery or reading fails closed.

recovery.detail: Correct unreadable files or unsupported policy paths; fresh healthy sampler observations recover through the existing hysteresis window.
